title: Pre-tinker measurements + session-view command-count evidence for the 2026-06-13T06:00Z decider run
purpose: Operator-side lightweight option (a) executed to give tinker focused signal: lints + test.js measured in isolation, plus the live session-view command-count breakdown that the operator captured from the actual run. This shortens tinker's Q2/Q3 investigation by ruling out the script-cost hypothesis.
key_finding: Lints + test.js are NOT the runtime bottleneck. Total per-push hook chain cost is ~1 second wall-clock. The dominant contributor is tool-call COUNT during decider's session — operator counted approximately 133 tool calls in the 2026-06-13T06:00Z run from the session view (see breakdown below). At a typical Opus tool-call round-trip of ~5-15 seconds (LLM inference + tool execution + network), 133 calls account for 11-33 minutes — which matches the observed 32-min runtime. The optimization target is tool-call CONSOLIDATION (parallel batching, fewer ledger micro-operations), not script execution.

isolated_script_timings.measurement_method: time node <script> on a fresh /tmp clone at HEAD, executed by operator-cowork-session 2026-06-13T07:10Z

scripts.name: node test.js
scripts.notes: 3831 tests pass; ~50 microseconds/test. Not a bottleneck.

scripts.name: node monitor/scripts/lint-required-artifacts.js --required 'monitor/integrity/prune-integrity-runs/run-*.json'
scripts.notes: Slowest of the lints due to git operations; still sub-second.

isolated_script_timings.implication: Even invoked 5 times per run (one per push attempt), the lint chain accounts for <10 seconds of the 32-minute runtime. Q2/Q3 of the directive can be deprioritized — lints and test.js are not the lever.

archive_file_sizes_at_audit_ts.note: closed-issues.json at 3.0 MB is the largest live JSON; lints that load it (lint-decider-surfaces for cross-file ISS uniqueness check, PROP-022 archive readers) pay an in-memory cost. expansion-tracker-archive.jsonl at 516 KB is the largest JSONL — if any decider intake reader scans it full instead of tail-only, that compounds across runs.

session_view_command_count_breakdown.source: Operator captured this from the live cowork-session view of decider-2026-06-13T10-00 (lastRunAt 06:03:59Z, summary commit 43921db 06:35:58Z)

phases_in_order.notes: PRELUDE setup includes fresh clone, PAT extraction, working-tree-population check, identity config. Some of this is unavoidable per run.

node test.js + build.js + verify + commit-prep. test.js itself is 0.18s; the 5 commands here are setup/verify, not test execution.

phases_in_order.phase: Open-issues ledger work (alloc IDs + close ISS-2728 + create ISS-2736/7/8)
phases_in_order.notes: 22 tool calls for ledger ops is the standout. Each alloc-id / read / modify / write / lint is a separate tool call. Strong candidate for consolidation.
18 calls for one self-apply + multi-ledger update. Similar pattern to the open-issues phase.

25 calls for a single commit + push suggests multiple `git pull --rebase` retries due to concurrent workspace-sync/dome-mirror pushes at :00/:30/etc. on a busy active-window hour. Strong evidence for Q5 (rebase churn).

tool_call_overhead_estimate.fit: Top end of the range matches observed. Tool-call count is consistent with the dominant contributor.

narrowed_questions_for_tinker: Q-Narrow-1 (from Q5 + commit-and-push 25-call phase): Is the 25-call commit-and-push phase dominated by rebase retries (workspace-sync :00 + dome-mirror :30 ⊕ decider 06:00 active-window overlap)? If yes, the fix is push-window coordination — e.g., dome-mirror pauses :30 when decider lastRunAt is within active 30min window, or decider holds its push until the next minute-bucket clear of other agents.

Q-Narrow-2 (from the 22-call open-issues ledger phase): Can the ledger micro-ops be consolidated into a single transactional helper? E.g., the alloc-N-IDs + close-1 + create-3 + lint-then-commit sequence could be one helper script that does all of it in-process, replacing ~15 of the 22 tool calls. Risk: cross-file ISS uniqueness check (PROP-089) must still fire — the helper would re-invoke it.

Q-Narrow-3 (from the 14-call read-context phase): Are the 14 sequential context reads parallelizable in a single tool-message batch? If decider's prompt currently issues them one-by-one (read-then-react pattern), a `read these 14 files in parallel` instruction at intake could halve the elapsed time.
constraints_unchanged_from_directive: PROP-083/087/089 enforcement must remain — they're load-bearing.
Honor the other-side: 32-min on this specific run included EXP-620 (substantive integration); proof requires multi-day trend (Q1 in the directive).
